newsitem.title: THAILAND: Cambodia loyalists retake key town - Thai army source.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia loyalists retake key town - Thai army source.

text.p: Troops loyal to ousted first Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh have retaken a key town in Cambodia's northwest shortly after losing it to forces from rival co-premier Hun Sen, a Thai army officer said on Monday.
Officials of Hun Sen's government in Phnom Penh confirmed fighting overnight but denied losing control of the town of Samrong, which they said they entered on Friday and fully controlled by Sunday.
"Last night there was fighting there," Secretary of State for Information Khieu Kanharith said on Monday. "But the government is still in control."
He had no information on casualties.

The Thai army officer, based in northwestern Thailand near the border with Cambodia, said the fighting was near strategically-placed Samrong town, about 30 km (20 miles) from the border where troops clashed on Sunday, he said.
He said that late on Sunday troops loyal to Second Prime Minister Hun Sen were dispersed by royalist troops, the officer said.
"We can still hear gunfire this morning inside Cambodia, but we don't know how heavy the fighting is," the officer told Reuters.
Hun Sen ousted Ranariddh in a coup just over two weeks ago after driving the prince's forces from Phnom Penh, but sporadic fighting between the two sides has continued in the country's northwest.
The Japanese Embassy said on Monday a Japanese man had gone missing in the area as Hun Sen's troops retreated.
Civilians from the northwest who have fled the conflict were waiting at the border hoping to cross into Thailand, the Thai army officer said.
"The border points are still closed because of the fighting. Cambodian people are waiting to cross the border to flee into Thailand. We will let them cross if the fighting gets worse," he said.
